patch.description:
Manual landed-cost entry (P5-4) - COGS, shipping, and other fees are
independent and all optional, so a merchant can enter just what they
know rather than being forced to fill in every component before any
cost data is usable. Only fields actually present in the request body
are updated - omitting a field leaves its current value alone, so a
second call can add e.g. shipping_cost without re-sending cogs.

post.description:
Manual competitor-price entry (P5-5) - no scraping infrastructure or
paid price-tracking API exists in this environment, so a merchant
records what they observed themselves, same "manual entry" choice as
P5-4's landed cost.

post.description:
Manually kicks off a fresh computation instead of waiting for the
8-hour scheduled tick - the same Celery task the store-connect trigger
already uses (app/tasks/dashboard_tasks.py), just fired on demand.
Fire-and-forget: the frontend polls GET /dashboard afterwards for the
new snapshot rather than this endpoint blocking on it.

post.description:
Backtests a prediction against real sales that have since happened -
see app/services/forecast.py::evaluate_prediction for the "in-sample
fit" vs "actual held-out accuracy" distinction this exists for.

Monte Carlo demand simulation around an existing forecast - reuses
its point_forecast as the day-by-day mean (so the simulation's center
always matches what the Forecasts page shows for this same prediction,
promo uplift and net-of-returns adjustment included) rather than
refitting a separate model from raw history. See app/ml/simulation.py.

Probability of running out of stock on or before each day of this
prediction's horizon, given current_stock (falls back to the product's
own stock_quantity if not provided). Grounded in the same forecast as
/simulate - see app/ml/simulation.py::simulate_stockout_probability.

Reorder point, safety stock, and order-up-to level for this product,
grounded in the same forecast as /simulate and /stockout. lead_time_days
defaults to a flat 7 (see app/ml/simulation.py) - neither this schema
nor the old app has per-product/supplier lead-time data, so it's a
request parameter rather than invented per-product data.

Grid-searches (reorder_point, reorder_quantity) combinations with a
real day-by-day simulation per candidate, rather than the closed-form
formula /inventory-recommendation uses - see
app/ml/simulation.py::optimize_inventory_policy for the search space.
Tie-break among candidates meeting the target service level minimizes
dollars tied up when P5-4's landed cost has been entered for this
product, falling back to smallest-reorder-quantity otherwise.

schema.title: Response List Promos Api V1 Stores  Store Id  Promos Get

get.description:
Price elasticity of demand, estimated from real transaction-price
variation in this product's order history (promotions, discounts,
genuine price changes) - see app/ml/elasticity.py for the method and
app/ml/data.py::build_product_price_quantity_series for how that
price signal is derived (this schema has no dedicated price-history
table). Returns 400 if there isn't enough price variation yet to
estimate anything meaningful - a real gate, not a soft warning, so a
caller can't be misled by a coefficient fit on a handful of noisy
points.

post.description:
Recommends a price under the chosen strategy. Defaults to
maximize_revenue (not the old app's maximize_profit default) since
cost-dependent strategies need a real per-unit cost - see
app/ml/pricing.py's module docstring - which isn't set for most
products until P5-4's cost entry exists; those strategies still work
here if you pass cost_override or once a cost has been entered.
Falls back to an assumed elasticity (clearly flagged via
elasticity_confidence) when there isn't enough price history to
measure a real one yet - a recommendation is still useful without
one, unlike the raw /elasticity endpoint above.

Projects the expected volume/revenue/profit impact of a specific
proposed price, without committing to it - "what if I priced this at
$X" rather than "what should I price this at".

Recommendations across every priced product in the store, ranked by
expected profit change (falling back to revenue change when cost data
isn't available) - products a cost-dependent strategy can't produce a
recommendation for are silently skipped, not failed, same convention
as P4-3's bulk reorder-alerts endpoint.

post.description:
Soft-launch tool: an admin creates a full account and grants it a
plan directly, with no payment - for beta users who shouldn't have to
pay yet, but should get real, working access rather than a workaround.
Restricted to ADMIN/SUPER_ADMIN (require_admin_write_role) since this
is financially consequential in a way SUPPORT/READ_ONLY staff
shouldn't be able to trigger.

Admin-triggered equivalent of the self-serve GDPR delete-account
flow (privacy.py's delete_my_account) - same anonymize-and-purge
semantics (see account_privacy.delete_account's own docstring for
why this isn't a hard row delete), just admin-attributed. Requires
typing the account's own email as payload.confirm_email, same
server-side check as the self-serve endpoint - not just a frontend
gate, since a direct API call could otherwise skip it. Gated behind
require_admin_write_role, same as every other mutating action in this
file (list_accounts/get_account are the only ones still on the plain
get_current_admin, since viewing account data is read-only) -
SUPPORT/READ_ONLY staff must not be able to trigger any of these,
impersonation included: it grants full read/write on the target
tenant's own data, a strictly bigger blast radius than the "business
data" write access require_tenant_write_access gates elsewhere.
